title: Substance Abuse and Risky Behaviour
summary: Factors behind risky behaviour, the effects of substance abuse on the individual, family and society, links between substance use, unsafe sex and violence, and strategies for prevention and getting help.

notes.text: Why do young people take risks?

items: **Peer pressure** and the wish to fit in.
The developing **teenage brain**: the area that controls planning and impulse control matures last (in the mid-20s).
**Easy availability** of alcohol and drugs; adults who model substance use.
**Media** that glamorises drinking, smoking and vaping.

rows: Addiction, mental health problems, poor school results, accidents, risky sex, crime, damage to the brain, liver, lungs and heart
Conflict, financial strain, broken trust, neglect, violence
Crime, road deaths, pressure on health services, lost productivity, gang activity

notes.label: The link between risks
notes.text: Alcohol and drugs lower inhibitions and impair judgement, making unprotected sex, sexual assault, violence and drunk driving much more likely. One risk often leads to others.

notes.title: Sorting effects
notes.problem: Sort: liver damage; dropping out of school; fighting with family; loss of income.
notes.answer: One effect each: physical, educational, social and economic.

items: Strong refusal skills and healthy self-esteem.
Involvement in sport, culture and community activities.
Accurate knowledge about the effects of substances.

notes.title: Building protection
notes.problem: Name three protective factors for a teenager.
notes.answer: Supportive adults, activities and positive friends.

items: **SANCA** (South African National Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence): counselling and treatment.
School counsellors, clinics and support groups (Narcotics Anonymous, Alcoholics Anonymous).
Treatment often involves detoxification, counselling and long-term support to prevent relapse.
